plus.analyst_notes:
Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/21482
Partner_Breach tag noted but the provider rule was NOT applied: GitLab (the company) was not breached; the attacker exploited a vulnerability in GitLab software that Byte Federal ran, so Byte Federal is the primary victim (same reasoning as the Oracle PeopleSoft/Nottingham record).
Coded hacking Exploit vuln via Web application, assets S - Code repository (GitLab) and S - Web application. Data: names, addresses, phones, emails, DOB, government IDs, SSNs, photos -> Personal (58,000 = data_total), Sensitive Personal (customer photographs/biometric-style images; reviewer may drop), transaction activity -> Bank. data_disclosure Potentially: the notice says the party 'may have had access' to the data. Motive Unknown.
Discovery internal Unknown (Byte Federal 'learned of' it Nov 18). Timeline: breach Sept 30 2024, discovered Nov 18 -> discovery 7 weeks. Victim NAICS 522320, Florida; headcount Unknown. dbir_year 2025.

summary: On September 30, 2024 an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in GitLab, used by Bitcoin ATM operator Byte Federal, to access its servers; Byte Federal discovered the intrusion on November 18. Data of about 58,000 customers may have been accessed, including names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, dates of birth, government-issued IDs, Social Security numbers, transaction activity and photographs. Byte Federal shut down its platform, reset all customer accounts and passwords and notified customers on December 12.
